items.pronunciation_notes: Two short syllables, nayaa, with the stress even across both.

learn.explanation_en: नया means new, and it is the one adjective in this module whose forms do not follow the pattern exactly. Where बड़ा gives बड़ी and बड़े, नया gives नई and नए — the य disappears rather than staying put. The regularised forms नयी and नये do turn up in older writing, but नई and नए are what you should learn and use.

examples.note: The feminine drops the य entirely rather than adding -ी to it.
The masculine plural does the same.
Only the masculine singular keeps the य.

common_error.why_en: The regular pattern would give नयी, but this adjective is irregular and the standard feminine is नई.

practice.question: नया
practice.explanation_en: नया is new. पुराना is old, of things rather than people.

game.question_en: ___ किताब — which form of नया fits?
game.explanation_en: किताब is feminine, and this adjective is irregular: the standard form is नई rather than the regular-looking नयी.

items.pronunciation_notes: Three syllables, puraanaa, with the middle vowel long and the first short.

learn.explanation_en: पुराना means old, but only of things. For a person you need बूढ़ा, which means aged, or बड़ा, which means elder. Calling someone पुराना would suggest they had been in use for a while. It ends in -ा and inflects regularly: पुराना, पुरानी, पुराने.

practice.question: पुराना
practice.explanation_en: पुराना is old, of things. For a person you would use बूढ़ा instead.

game.question_en: ___ घर — which form of पुराना fits?
game.explanation_en: घर is masculine and singular, so पुराना keeps its -ा form.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted फ़ is an f sound, and the final vowel drops: saaf, one syllable.

learn.explanation_en: साफ़ means clean, and also clear — साफ़ पानी is clean water while साफ़ बात is plain speaking. It ends in a consonant, so it never changes form. This word has appeared in examples in almost every level of this module, always in exactly this shape, which is the whole point of an invariable adjective.

examples.note: घर is masculine, and the form is unchanged.
मेज़ is feminine, and it is still unchanged.

practice.question: साफ़
practice.explanation_en: साफ़ is clean, and by extension clear or plain.

game.question_en: ___ मेज़ — which form of साफ़ fits?
game.explanation_en: साफ़ ends in a consonant and never changes, so the same form serves a feminine noun as a masculine one.

summary.recap_en: This level added नया, पुराना and साफ़. नया is the one irregular adjective here, giving नई and नए rather than the forms the pattern would predict.
summary.next_up_en: Next: गरम, ठंडा and गंदा — one invariable and two that inflect.

items.pronunciation_notes: The final vowel drops, giving garam in two syllables, and र is a single tap.

learn.explanation_en: गरम covers both hot and warm, since Hindi does not separate the two the way English does. It ends in a consonant and never changes form. You will also see it spelt गर्म, with the reph, and both spellings are correct and equally common — the pronunciation is identical.

examples.note: चाय is feminine, and गरम is unchanged.
पानी is masculine, and the form is the same.
Unchanged again, as it always is.

practice.question: गरम
practice.explanation_en: गरम is hot or warm — Hindi uses one word for both.

game.question_en: ___ चाय — which form of गरम fits?
game.explanation_en: गरम never changes form. गरमी is a separate noun meaning heat or summer, not a feminine version of this adjective.

items.pronunciation_notes: An aspirated retroflex ठ, and the dot before ड is read as the retroflex nasal: ṭhaṇḍaa.

learn.explanation_en: ठंडा means cold, and unlike its opposite गरम it ends in -ा and inflects: ठंडा, ठंडी, ठंडे. That asymmetry is worth noticing — there is no rule saying opposites behave alike. The word opens with an aspirated retroflex and carries an anusvara read as the retroflex nasal, so it is a small pronunciation exercise as well.

examples.note: चाय is feminine, so -ी — where गरम would not have changed.

practice.question: ठंडा
practice.explanation_en: ठंडा is cold. गरम is its opposite, and it does not inflect.

game.question_en: ___ पानी — which form of ठंडा fits?
game.explanation_en: पानी is masculine, so ठंडा keeps its -ा form. ठंड on its own is a noun meaning cold weather.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dot before द is read as a plain dental n, so the word is gandaa.

learn.explanation_en: गंदा means dirty, and it is the opposite of साफ़. Once again the pair splits: साफ़ never changes while गंदा inflects as गंदा, गंदी, गंदे. The anusvara here sits before द, a dental, so it is read as a plain n rather than the retroflex ṇ heard in ठंडा.

practice.question: गंदा
practice.explanation_en: गंदा is dirty. साफ़ is its opposite, and it does not inflect.

game.question_en: ___ कमीज़ — which form of गंदा fits?
game.explanation_en: कमीज़ is feminine, so गंदा becomes गंदी.

summary.recap_en: This level covered गरम, ठंडा and गंदा. Both pairs of opposites here are mismatched — गरम and साफ़ never change while ठंडा and गंदा inflect — so being an opposite tells you nothing about the ending.
summary.next_up_en: Next: खाली, भारी and लंबा, including two adjectives that end in -ी and still never change.

items.pronunciation_notes: Aspirated ख with a clear puff of air, then two long vowels: khaalii.

learn.explanation_en: खाली means empty, and also vacant or free — a खाली कुर्सी is an unoccupied chair and खाली समय is free time. It ends in -ी, and this is where नारंगी's lesson pays off: adjectives ending in -ी do not inflect. Only the -ा ending triggers agreement, so खाली is fixed no matter what follows it.

examples.note: कमरा is masculine, and खाली is unchanged.
कुर्सी is feminine, and it is still unchanged.
Also feminine, and the form does not move.

practice.question: खाली
practice.explanation_en: खाली is empty, and also vacant or free.

game.question_en: ___ कुर्सी — which form of खाली fits?
game.explanation_en: खाली ends in -ी, and adjectives with that ending never inflect — there is no masculine form to build.

items.pronunciation_notes: Breathy भ — one sound, not b then h — and a single tap for र: bhaarii.

learn.explanation_en: भारी means heavy, in weight and also figuratively — a भारी आवाज़ is a deep voice. Like खाली it ends in -ी and never changes form. Two invariable -ी adjectives in one level is deliberate: this ending catches learners out repeatedly, because it looks exactly like the feminine marker on nouns.

examples.note: किताब is feminine, and भारी is unchanged.
Feminine again, with no change at all.

practice.question: भारी
practice.explanation_en: भारी is heavy. It also describes a deep voice.

game.question_en: ___ किताब — which form of भारी fits?
game.explanation_en: भारी ends in -ी and never inflects, so this is the only form it has.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dot before ब is read as m, because ब is made with the lips: lambaa.

learn.explanation_en: लंबा covers both long and tall, so it works for a road and for a person alike. It ends in -ा and inflects: लंबा, लंबी, लंबे. The anusvara before ब is read as m, since ब is made with the lips — the same rule that made रंग an ng and अंडा a retroflex nasal.

practice.question: लंबा
practice.explanation_en: लंबा is long, and also tall when describing a person.

game.question_en: ___ उँगली — which form of लंबा fits?
game.explanation_en: उँगली is feminine, so लंबा becomes लंबी.

summary.recap_en: This level put two invariable -ी adjectives side by side with an inflecting -ा one. खाली and भारी look as though they carry a feminine ending and never move, while लंबा takes all three forms.
summary.next_up_en: Next: सुंदर, सस्ता and महँगा complete the fifteen adjectives.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dot before द is a plain dental n, and the final vowel drops: sundar in two syllables.

learn.explanation_en: सुंदर means beautiful, and it is used of people, places and things alike. It ends in a consonant, so it never changes form. Note that सुंदरी exists as a separate noun meaning a beautiful woman — it is not the feminine of this adjective, and using it that way would be a mistake.

examples.note: चिड़िया is feminine, and सुंदर is unchanged.
घर is masculine, and the form is the same.

practice.question: सुंदर
practice.explanation_en: सुंदर is beautiful, and it works for people, places and things.

game.question_en: ___ चिड़िया — which form of सुंदर fits?
game.explanation_en: सुंदर never changes. सुंदरी is a separate noun, not a feminine form of the adjective.

items.pronunciation_notes: The स्त stack runs स straight into त with no vowel between: sastaa, two syllables.

learn.explanation_en: सस्ता means cheap or inexpensive, without the negative edge English sometimes gives the word — it is simply a good price. It ends in -ा and inflects regularly. The स्त stack from Module 3 sits in the middle, both halves dental, so the tongue stays on the teeth throughout.

practice.question: सस्ता
practice.explanation_en: सस्ता is cheap in the sense of inexpensive, with no suggestion of poor quality.

game.question_en: ___ जूता — which form of सस्ता fits?
game.explanation_en: जूता is masculine and singular, so सस्ता keeps its -ा form.

items.pronunciation_notes: The crescent nasalises the middle vowel and adds no n sound of its own: mahãgaa.

learn.explanation_en: महँगा means expensive, the opposite of सस्ता, and it inflects the same way. The crescent in the middle nasalises the vowel without adding a consonant, so there is no n to be heard. You will also see it written महंगा with the plain dot, which is very common in print — the two spellings are read identically.

practice.question: महँगा
practice.explanation_en: महँगा is expensive. सस्ता is its opposite, and both inflect.

game.question_en: ___ साड़ी — which form of महँगा fits?
game.explanation_en: साड़ी is feminine, so महँगा becomes महँगी.

summary.recap_en: This level completed the fifteen adjectives. Nine of them end in -ा and take three forms, while साफ़, गरम, खाली, भारी, सुंदर and नारंगी never change — and खाली and भारी prove that a -ी ending is no guarantee of anything.
summary.next_up_en: Next: places in town, starting with the market and the shops in it.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted ज़ is a z sound, and the final vowel drops: baazaar in two syllables.

learn.explanation_en: बाज़ार is a market, and in practice the whole shopping area of a town rather than a single covered building. It is masculine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable, and the plural does not change. English borrowed the word as 'bazaar', keeping the z sound that the dot marks.

examples.note: बड़ा takes -ा because बाज़ार is masculine.
The place comes before the verb.

practice.question: बाज़ार
practice.explanation_en: बाज़ार is a market or shopping area. दुकान is a single shop within it.

game.question_en: राम ___ बाज़ार — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: बाज़ार is masculine, so का. Its consonant ending gives no clue.

items.pronunciation_notes: Dental द with the tongue on the teeth, and the final vowel drops: dukaan.

learn.explanation_en: दुकान is a shop, from the smallest stall upwards. It is feminine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable — and it sits inside a बाज़ार, which is masculine, so a single sentence about shopping can easily need both forms. The plural is दुकानें.

examples.note: छोटा takes -ी because दुकान is feminine.
की agrees with दुकान, the word that follows it.

common_error.why_en: दुकान is feminine, so the adjective takes -ी — while बाज़ार, in the same setting, takes -ा.

practice.question: दुकान
practice.explanation_en: दुकान is a single shop. बाज़ार is the whole market area.

game.question_en: राम ___ दुकान — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: दुकान is feminine, so की. Its consonant ending predicts nothing.

items.pronunciation_notes: The flap ड़ — the tongue curls back and flicks forward — and the final vowel drops: saṛak.

learn.explanation_en: सड़क is a road or street. It is feminine and ends in a consonant, so the gender has to be learned. The word contains the flap ड़ from Module 2, and notice what happens in the plural: सड़क is saṛak but सड़कें is saṛkeṁ, with the middle vowel dropping once the ending is added — the same behaviour as बहन and बहनें.

examples.note: लंबा takes -ी because सड़क is feminine.
The middle vowel drops in the plural.

practice.question: सड़क
practice.explanation_en: सड़क is a road or street, the kind vehicles use.

game.question_en: राम ___ सड़क — का, के or की?

summary.recap_en: This level began the places with बाज़ार, दुकान and सड़क. All three end in consonants and none of them announces its gender, so all three are flagged.
summary.next_up_en: Next: more places in town, including the school, the hospital and the station.
